notes:
Summary: evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) as primary inference platform for regulated trading desk analytics and downstream customer communications. Primary ask is enterprise-grade audit logging: full request/response metadata export to Splunk SIEM, immutable logs, and 7-year retention for forensic & regulatory purposes.

Key quotes from stakeholders: "We need signed, tamper-evident logs pushed to our Splunk with field-level mapping — every call must have tenant_id + request_id + model_version + token metrics" — Head of Compliance.

Audit logging requirements (detailed):
- SIEM export: prefer push to Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) over TLS with mTLS option; fallback S3-bucket delivery + Kinesis Firehose acceptable for bulk archival.
- Formats: want canonical JSON events (RFC5424-like envelope) and optional CEF for integrations. Customer will do field-mapping on their side but requires stable keys.
- Schema (requested minimal fields): timestamp, request_id, tenant_id, route, model_name, model_version, input_hash (sha256), output_hash (sha256), prompt_token_count, completion_token_count, latency_ms, kv_cache_hits, decision_flags (safety_blocked|modified), user_pseudonym_id, src_ip_v4, src_region, response_size_bytes, error_code, storage_reference (if archived).
- Access logs & auth: capture SSO subject (pseudonymized), token_type (service/account), session_id, and auth_delegation_chain for any impersonation.
- Integrity & signing: customer requires HMAC signing of log batches and support for signed envelopes (or ability to push to an HSM-backed collector).
- Retention: regulatory ask = 7 years for audit logs, 3 years for transaction-level artifacts, 90 days hot for quick query. Need lifecycle: hot (90d) -> cold (up to 3y) -> archive (up to 7y). Must support legal-hold overrides.
- Encryption: logs at rest encrypted with customer-managed keys (BYOK) using AWS KMS / Azure KeyVault. Key rotation policy must not invalidate previously archived logs; Redwood needs to support envelope encryption and re-wrap operations.
- Access controls: RBAC for log access, audit trail for who downloaded/exported logs, integration with customer SIEM RBAC preferred.

Technical discussion notes / POC scope:
- POC will run in their VPC with private-control-plane endpoint. Goal: 2-week ingest of synthetic traffic to validate SIEM export and schema mapping.
- Redwood to deliver sample export: 10k events in JSON + 10k in CEF, plus mapping CSV to Palisade SIEM fields.
- Validate latency metrics, token accounting, and the signed-batch workflow to HEC over mTLS.
- KMS: Palisade requires BYOK via external key import; need confirmation on Redwood's key policy support and HSM-backed signing for log integrity.

Timeline & recent activity:
- 2026-01-20: intro call (AE + SE) — scope captured, initial security checklist sent.
- 2026-02-02: compliance deep-dive with Head of Compliance; asked for legal retention justification.
- 2026-02-18: infra kickoff (fireflies ff_2026-02-18_palisade_kickoff) — discussed VPC peering, NAT, private endpoints.
- 2026-02-25: security deep dive (fireflies ff_2026-02-25_security_deepdive) — SIEM/export options and KMS questions surfaced.
- 2026-03-04: SE demo of private control plane; Palisade requested SIEM mapping template and BYOK integration spec.

Open questions for Redwood:
- Can Redwood sign log batches with customer's HSM keys or provide an HSM-backed forwarder?
- Does Redwood support legal-hold lifecycle operations by customer admins?
- Confirm encryption re-wrap strategy for long-term archives when keys rotate.

Next steps (short):
- Deliver SIEM mapping template and sample payloads (action: Redwood SE, due 2026-03-08).
- Technical workshop with Palisade infra + Redwood infra to validate HEC + mTLS (schedule wk of 2026-03-15).
- Legal to draft retention addendum for 7-year archive (owner: Palisade legal).

Sales notes / positioning: enterprise revenue opportunity if BYOK + 7yr retention supported; high ARR and reference case for regulated finance vertical. POC success criteria: log integrity, SIEM compatibility, seamless KMS BYOK flow, and no more than 200ms added end-to-end median latency for logged requests.
